head: Zombies Aren't Real game: zombie defense on real city maps for iPhone
dek: Zombies Aren't Real is a $4.99 strategy game where you fight a zombie outbreak on maps built from real-world map data, street by street. It came out on 23 November and was #73 among paid apps on the US App Store on 25 November.
details: You place snipers, turrets, mortars and garrisons, call in air strikes and build safe zones and gates to shelter civilians. It's single-player with no account needed. The maps come from public data such as OpenStreetMap. It's made by Jordan O'Leary and runs on iPhone and iPad.
where: iPhone and iPad, $4.99 on the App Store
means: If you like tower defense games, this one lets you defend a real city instead of a made-up map.
todo: Find Zombies Aren't Real on the App Store; it's a one-time purchase listed at $4.99.
